newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Soviet economic reform pioneer Shatalin dies at 62.
newsitem.headline: Soviet economic reform pioneer Shatalin dies at 62.

text.p: Soviet economist Stanislav Shatalin, pioneer of some of the first cautious economic reforms in the Soviet Union, died on Monday aged 62, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Tass quoted the Reform Foundation, which Shatalin had headed since 1990, as saying he died suddenly in Moscow. Officials at the foundation were not immediately available for comment.

In late 1989 Shatalin joined Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev in his "perestroika" campaign to reform the communist political system and the centrally planned economy without dumping its basic social values and principles.

But a year later, disillusioned with the official programme, Shatalin got together with the young and ambitious politician Grigory Yavlinsky to draw up what became known as the "500 days" plan for a crash conversion from socialism to a market economy.
Gorbachev rejected the plan, but Russian President Boris Yeltsin later incorporated many elements of it into the economic reform programme he launched in 1992.
